title: Kubernetes & kubectl
description: Beginner-to-advanced Kubernetes reference covering architecture, API objects, Pods, workloads, Services, configuration, storage, health, resources, scheduling, scaling, security, observability, kubectl, Kustomize, Helm, and production operations.

sections.title: Cluster & API Mental Model
sections.description: Kubernetes continuously reconciles declared desired state through API objects and controllers.

subtopics.title: Control Plane, Nodes & Reconciliation
subtopics.description: The API server validates/persists intent; scheduler assigns unscheduled Pods; controllers reconcile objects; kubelets and runtimes realize Pods on nodes.

diagram.content:
flowchart LR
  U[kubectl / controllers] --> A[API server]
  A <--> E[etcd]
  A --> S[Scheduler]
  A --> C[Controllers]
  A --> K[Kubelet on node]
  K --> R[Container runtime]
  C -. reconcile desired vs actual .-> A

callouts.title: Do Not Manage Pods Like Servers
callouts.text: Change the owning Deployment/StatefulSet configuration and let reconciliation replace Pods. Manual Pod fixes are ephemeral and fight controllers.

subtopics.title: apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec & status
subtopics.description: spec declares desired state; controllers write observed status. metadata names, namespaces, labels, annotations, owner references, finalizers, and generation enable management.

codeBlocks.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api
  namespace: shop
  labels: { app.kubernetes.io/name: api }
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector: { matchLabels: { app.kubernetes.io/name: api } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app.kubernetes.io/name: api } }
    spec:
      containers: [{ name: api, image: registry.example/api@sha256:... }]

callouts.title: Selectors Are Contracts
callouts.text: Workload and Service selectors must match intended Pod labels. Immutable/mistyped selectors can orphan workloads or route traffic to the wrong application.

subtopics.title: Declarative Apply, Field Ownership & Diff
subtopics.description: Store desired configuration in version control, review server-side diff, and use one consistent field manager/workflow per field set.

codeBlocks.code:
kubectl diff --server-side -f manifests/
kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=platform-cd -f manifests/
kubectl get deployment api -n shop -o yaml
kubectl explain deployment.spec.template.spec.containers.resources
kubectl api-resources

callouts.title: Avoid Imperative Drift
callouts.text: kubectl edit/scale/set can be useful in incidents but must be reconciled back to Git/source of truth or the next deployment will overwrite the change.

sections.title: Pods & Workload Controllers
sections.description: Select a controller based on identity, rollout, scheduling, and completion semantics.

subtopics.title: Pods, Init Containers & Sidecars
subtopics.description: Containers in a Pod share network namespace and volumes, are scheduled together, and share lifecycle fate. Init containers complete in order before app startup; sidecars support the app when coupling is justified.

codeBlocks.code:
spec:
  initContainers:
    - name: migrate-check
      image: app-tools@sha256:...
      command: ["./wait-for-schema"]
  containers:
    - name: api
      image: app@sha256:...
      ports: [{ name: http, containerPort: 8080 }]
    - name: proxy
      image: proxy@sha256:...

callouts.title: One Pod Means One Scaling Unit
callouts.text: Do not place unrelated services in one Pod. Every container scales, schedules, restarts, and consumes resources together.

subtopics.title: Deployments & Rolling Updates
subtopics.description: Deployment manages ReplicaSets for stateless interchangeable Pods and supports rolling replacement, history, pause/resume, and rollback.

codeBlocks.code:
spec:
  replicas: 4
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate: { maxUnavailable: 0, maxSurge: 1 }
  minReadySeconds: 10
  progressDeadlineSeconds: 600
  template:
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30

callouts.title: Zero Downtime Requires Application Support
callouts.text: Readiness, graceful SIGTERM/drain, compatible database changes, sufficient capacity, and external dependency behavior determine availability—not rollout settings alone.

subtopics.title: StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job & CronJob
subtopics.description: StatefulSet provides stable identity/storage ordering; DaemonSet runs per eligible node; Job completes finite work; CronJob creates Jobs on a schedule.

table.title: Kubernetes Workload Controller Selection
rows: Ephemeral pod identity; shared or external storage
Stable ordinal, DNS identity, and per-pod claims
Log, metrics, networking, and security agents
Runs pods until a finite completion target
History governed by job retention settings

codeBlocks.code:
Deployment → replaceable replicas and rolling web/services
StatefulSet → stable network/storage identity; app handles replication
DaemonSet → node agent such as logging/network/security
Job → finite completion with retry/backoff semantics
CronJob → scheduled Job creation; define concurrencyPolicy and deadlines

callouts.title: Cron Schedules Can Duplicate or Miss
callouts.text: Jobs must be idempotent, concurrency-aware, and observable. Kubernetes scheduling is not an exactly-once transaction system.

sections.title: Services, DNS & External Traffic
sections.description: Use stable discovery and explicit traffic policy over ephemeral Pod IPs.

subtopics.title: Service Types & EndpointSlices
subtopics.description: A Service selects ready backends and exposes a stable virtual IP/DNS. ClusterIP is internal; NodePort and LoadBalancer expose through node/provider mechanisms; ExternalName aliases DNS.

codeBlocks.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: { name: api, namespace: shop }
spec:
  selector: { app.kubernetes.io/name: api }
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: http
  type: ClusterIP

callouts.title: Service Selects Labels, Not Deployment Names
callouts.text: Verify EndpointSlices after deployment. A Service with no endpoints usually means label mismatch or Pods failing readiness.

subtopics.title: Cluster DNS & NetworkPolicy
subtopics.description: Services receive DNS names; NetworkPolicy controls allowed ingress/egress when the CNI supports enforcement.

callouts.title: Default Deny Needs DNS/Egress Planning
callouts.text: Roll out policies with observability. Allow required DNS, identity, telemetry, and external dependencies; test the actual CNI semantics.

subtopics.title: Ingress, Gateway API & TLS
subtopics.description: Ingress or Gateway API configures an installed controller/provider to accept external traffic, terminate or pass TLS, and route by host/path.

codeBlocks.code:
Ingress: mature HTTP/HTTPS routing API implemented by an ingress controller
Gateway API: role-oriented GatewayClass/Gateway/Route model for richer routing
Service LoadBalancer: direct provider load balancer for one service
No controller installed → API objects alone do not create a working data plane

callouts.title: Trust Proxy Headers Deliberately
callouts.text: Configure known proxy hops, TLS redirect, allowed hosts, request/body/time limits, and certificate automation. Do not trust arbitrary forwarded identity/IP headers.

sections.title: Configuration, Secrets & Storage
sections.description: Separate non-secret configuration, confidential material, ephemeral space, and durable data.

subtopics.title: ConfigMap & Secret Consumption
subtopics.description: Mount as files or expose selected keys as environment variables. ConfigMap is non-confidential; Secret is base64-encoded API data and needs encryption/access controls.

callouts.title: Secret Is Not Automatically Secret
callouts.text: Enable encryption at rest, restrict RBAC, avoid broad env/log exposure, integrate an external secret system where needed, and rotate credentials. Base64 is not encryption.

subtopics.title: Volumes, PV, PVC & StorageClass
subtopics.description: Pod volumes provide shared/mounted storage; PVC requests durable capacity/access mode; PV represents provisioned storage; StorageClass drives dynamic provisioning and reclaim behavior.

codeBlocks.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: { name: data }
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: fast
  resources: { requests: { storage: 20Gi } }

callouts.title: Persistent Volume Is Not Backup
callouts.text: Test snapshots/backups and restore, reclaim policy, zone/node attachment, expansion, corruption, and application-consistent recovery.

subtopics.title: emptyDir, Projected & CSI Volumes
subtopics.description: emptyDir follows Pod lifetime; projected combines sources; CSI provides vendor storage and secret/config integrations with driver-specific semantics.

codeBlocks.code:
emptyDir → cache/scratch/shared Pod files; erased with Pod
emptyDir medium: Memory → tmpfs charged to memory
projected → combine Secret, ConfigMap, downward API, service-account token
CSI ephemeral/persistent → driver-managed; verify lifecycle and security
hostPath → node filesystem coupling; avoid for portable apps

callouts.title: Environment Values Do Not Hot Reload
callouts.text: Mounted ConfigMap/Secret files may update eventually, but env vars remain from process start. Applications must watch/reload files safely or roll Pods on configuration changes.

sections.title: Health, Resources & Scheduling
sections.description: Give the scheduler and kubelet truthful signals about capacity, startup, readiness, and failure.

subtopics.title: Startup, Readiness & Liveness Probes
subtopics.description: Startup delays other probes until initialized; readiness controls traffic; liveness restarts a stuck process. HTTP, TCP, exec, and gRPC mechanisms serve different contracts.

callouts.title: Do Not Make Liveness Depend on Every Dependency
callouts.text: Restarting all Pods because a database is down amplifies failure. Liveness answers whether this process is irrecoverably stuck; readiness may reflect inability to serve.

subtopics.title: Requests, Limits & QoS
subtopics.description: Requests drive scheduling and reserved capacity; limits constrain usage. CPU limit throttles; memory limit can cause OOM kill; QoS affects eviction priority.

callouts.title: Measure Working Set and Throttling
callouts.text: Arbitrary tiny limits create latency and OOM loops; absent requests cause overcommit/unpredictable scheduling. Size from production percentiles and load tests.

subtopics.title: Affinity, Taints, Topology & Disruption
subtopics.description: Use selectors/affinity for required or preferred placement, taints/tolerations for node admission, topology spread for failure domains, and PDB for voluntary disruptions.

codeBlocks.code:
topologySpreadConstraints:
  - maxSkew: 1
    topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
    whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
    labelSelector: { matchLabels: { app.kubernetes.io/name: api } }

# PDB: minAvailable: 2 or maxUnavailable: 1 for controller-managed replicas

callouts.title: PDB Does Not Protect Against Every Outage
callouts.text: It limits voluntary eviction, not crashes, node loss, bad rollouts, or application failure. Impossible budgets can block upgrades/drains.

sections.title: Scaling, Rollouts & Lifecycle
sections.description: Scale from useful signals and coordinate startup, traffic, termination, and schema compatibility.

subtopics.title: HPA, VPA & Cluster Autoscaling
subtopics.description: HPA changes replicas from resource/custom/external metrics; VPA recommends or adjusts Pod resources; node autoscaling supplies cluster capacity.

codeBlocks.code:
HPA needs resource requests for utilization metrics
Choose metrics correlated with work: queue depth, concurrency, latency—not only CPU
Set min/max, stabilization, and scale behavior
Avoid conflicting HPA and VPA control of the same resource dimension
Node provisioning is slower than Pod scaling; retain headroom

callouts.title: Autoscaling Cannot Fix a Saturated Dependency
callouts.text: More Pods can overload a database or queue. Bound concurrency, model downstream capacity, and load-test scaling/scale-down behavior.

subtopics.title: Graceful Termination & preStop
subtopics.description: On deletion, endpoints/readiness change and kubelet runs preStop then sends the stop signal within terminationGracePeriodSeconds. Applications must stop intake and drain.

codeBlocks.code:
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45
  containers:
    - name: api
      lifecycle:
        preStop:
          exec: { command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 5"] }

callouts.title: preStop Uses the Same Grace Budget
callouts.text: A long hook reduces time available for application shutdown. Prefer the app handling SIGTERM/readiness and use a hook only for a clear platform timing need.

subtopics.title: Rolling, Blue/Green & Canary
subtopics.description: Deployment natively performs rolling updates. Blue/green switches traffic between full stacks; canary shifts a fraction through separate workloads/routing and analysis.

codeBlocks.code:
Rolling → simple, mixed versions coexist temporarily
Blue/green → fast switch/rollback, double capacity, state compatibility required
Canary → limited exposure + metrics, needs traffic control and promotion automation
All strategies → backward-compatible APIs/events/schema and explicit rollback criteria

callouts.title: Database Rollback Is Separate
callouts.text: Use expand/migrate/contract changes and forward-compatible readers/writers. Rolling back application images does not automatically reverse data migrations.

sections.title: Security, Tenancy & Policy
sections.description: Protect the API, workload identity, runtime, network, images, and admission path.

subtopics.title: RBAC & Service Accounts
subtopics.description: Roles/ClusterRoles define verbs on resources; bindings grant them to users/groups/service accounts. Give each workload a narrow identity and disable token mounting when unused.

codeBlocks.code:
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata: { name: config-reader, namespace: shop }
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["configmaps"]
    resourceNames: ["api-runtime"]
    verbs: ["get"]

callouts.title: Avoid Wildcards and Broad Bindings
callouts.text: Do not grant cluster-admin, * resources/verbs, Secret list access, or default service accounts for convenience. Audit effective permissions and escalation paths.

subtopics.title: Pod Security Standards & securityContext
subtopics.description: Enforce restricted workload defaults: non-root, no privilege escalation, dropped capabilities, seccomp, read-only root where possible, and controlled UID/GID/volume ownership.

codeBlocks.code:
securityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 10001
  seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault }
containers:
  - name: api
    securityContext:
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }

callouts.title: Enforce at Admission
callouts.text: Namespace Pod Security Admission or policy engines prevent unsafe manifests before scheduling. CI lint alone cannot stop manual or compromised deploy clients.

subtopics.title: Image Policy, Namespaces, Quotas & Admission
subtopics.description: Use verified immutable images, namespace boundaries, ResourceQuota/LimitRange, network/pod policies, and admission validation/mutation.

codeBlocks.code:
Pin image digests and verify signatures/provenance
Restrict registries and mutable tags
Scan continuously and rebuild patched images
Use namespaces for organization, not sole hard multi-tenancy
Apply quotas/limits to prevent resource exhaustion
Protect admission webhooks for availability/failure policy
Audit API and workload actions

callouts.title: Namespace Is Not a Security Boundary Alone
callouts.text: RBAC, network policy, pod security, secrets, node isolation, quotas, and control-plane configuration must work together for tenant isolation.

sections.title: kubectl, Observability & Debugging
sections.description: Move from desired/observed object state to events, logs, metrics, traffic, process, and node evidence.

subtopics.title: Contexts, Get, Describe, Logs & Exec
subtopics.description: Always confirm context/namespace, query labels, inspect status/conditions/events, then enter a container only when needed.

codeBlocks.code:
kubectl config current-context
kubectl config get-contexts
kubectl get pods -n shop -l app.kubernetes.io/name=api -o wide
kubectl describe pod api-xyz -n shop
kubectl logs -n shop api-xyz -c api --previous --tail=200
kubectl exec -n shop -it api-xyz -c api -- sh
kubectl get events -n shop --sort-by=.lastTimestamp

callouts.title: Production Context Guard
callouts.text: Use distinct contexts/prompts, least-privilege credentials, explicit namespaces, and server-side dry-run/diff. Never paste destructive commands without resolving exact targets.

subtopics.title: Ephemeral Debug, Port Forward & Copy
subtopics.description: Ephemeral containers add diagnostics to a Pod without rebuilding minimal images; port-forward creates a temporary local tunnel; cp transfers files via container tooling assumptions.

codeBlocks.code:
kubectl debug -n shop -it pod/api-xyz --image=busybox:1.37 --target=api
kubectl run -n shop net-debug --rm -it --image=nicolaka/netshoot -- sh
kubectl port-forward -n shop service/api 8080:80
kubectl top pods -n shop
kubectl auth can-i get secrets -n shop --as=system:serviceaccount:shop:api

callouts.title: Debug Access Is Privileged
callouts.text: Ephemeral containers and port-forward can expose process/network/data access. Restrict RBAC, audit usage, and do not use port-forward as production connectivity.

subtopics.title: Pod Failure & Incident Triage
subtopics.description: Use status reason and conditions to select the next evidence source rather than restarting blindly.

codeBlocks.code:
Pending → scheduling events, requests, taints, affinity, PVC, quota
ImagePullBackOff → image name/digest, registry auth/network/policy
CrashLoopBackOff → current + --previous logs, exit code, config, probes, OOM
Running not Ready → readiness endpoint, Service endpoints, dependencies
OOMKilled → memory working set/limit/leak; don't only increase blindly
Evicted → node pressure, ephemeral storage/memory, requests
Traffic failure → DNS, EndpointSlice, selector, NetworkPolicy, gateway/controller
Rollout stuck → conditions, readiness, capacity, progress deadline

callouts.title: Events Expire
callouts.text: Collect centralized logs, metrics, traces, audit events, object state, and deployment annotations. Build runbooks before incidents and preserve a timeline.

sections.title: Kustomize, Helm & Delivery
sections.description: Render, review, validate, and reconcile configuration without hiding the resulting Kubernetes API objects.

subtopics.title: Kustomize Bases, Overlays & Generators
subtopics.description: Kustomize composes resources and patches without templating. kubectl supports render/apply with -k; generators add content hashes that trigger rollout references.

codeBlocks.code:
# overlays/production/kustomization.yaml
resources: [../../base]
namespace: shop-production
images:
  - name: registry.example/app
    newName: registry.example/app
    digest: sha256:...
patches:
  - path: replicas.yaml
configMapGenerator:
  - name: api-config
    literals: [LOG_LEVEL=info]

callouts.title: Render Before Apply
callouts.text: Run kubectl kustomize, schema/policy checks, and kubectl diff -k in CI. Keep overlays small; duplication often signals a missing base/component boundary.

subtopics.title: Helm Charts, Values & Releases
subtopics.description: Helm packages templated resources as charts and tracks releases. Values configure chart-supported choices; templates must render valid secure manifests.

codeBlocks.code:
helm lint ./chart
helm template shop ./chart -f values-production.yaml
helm diff upgrade shop ./chart -n shop -f values-production.yaml
helm upgrade --install shop ./chart -n shop --create-namespace --atomic --timeout 10m
helm history shop -n shop
helm rollback shop 3 -n shop

callouts.title: Template Output Is the Real API
callouts.text: Review rendered manifests, pin chart/dependency versions, validate schemas/policies, avoid secrets in values/history, and understand hooks/ownership before install.

subtopics.title: GitOps, Drift & Promotion
subtopics.description: A delivery controller can reconcile versioned desired state, expose drift and health, and promote immutable artifacts across environments.

codeBlocks.code:
Build once → scan/sign → push immutable digest
Update environment desired state through reviewed change
Render/validate/policy/diff before merge
Controller reconciles and reports health/drift
Promote the same digest; do not rebuild per environment
Automate rollback/roll-forward using measured gates
Emergency changes must be committed back to source of truth

callouts.title: Git Encryption Is Not Runtime Secret Management
callouts.text: If storing encrypted secrets in Git, protect keys and decrypted delivery paths. Prefer external secret references where operationally appropriate.

sections.title: Production Readiness Checklist
sections.description: Review workload correctness, capacity, availability, security, data, and operations as one system.

subtopics.title: Version Skew, Upgrades & API Deprecations
subtopics.description: Kubernetes 1.36 upgrades require supported component skew, compatible add-ons, reviewed API removals, and workload validation before control-plane and node rollout.

codeBlocks.code:
kubectl version
kubectl api-resources
kubectl get --raw /readyz?verbose
# Render manifests and scan deprecated APIs before upgrading
kubectl diff -k overlays/production

callouts.title: Upgrade One Supported Minor at a Time
callouts.text: Check the official skew policy and release notes for the exact source and target versions. Validate CNI, CSI, ingress/Gateway, metrics, admission webhooks, autoscaling, backup, and rollback procedures in a representative environment.

subtopics.title: Workload & Cluster Checklist
subtopics.description: A manifest is deployable only when its application and platform contracts are proven.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Images use verified immutable digests
□ Controller matches identity/completion semantics
□ Labels/selectors/Service EndpointSlices are correct
□ Startup/readiness/liveness probes answer distinct questions
□ Requests/limits/ephemeral storage derive from measurements
□ SIGTERM, drain, grace, and rollout settings are tested
□ Replicas spread across failure domains; disruption budget is feasible
□ Autoscaling uses meaningful metrics and respects dependencies
□ Config/Secret changes trigger or safely reload
□ Persistent data has backup, restore, migration, reclaim plans
□ Service accounts/RBAC/network/pod security are least privilege
□ Admission, image, quota, and namespace policies are enforced
□ Logs/metrics/traces/audit/deploy markers and alerts exist
□ Kustomize/Helm output is rendered, validated, diffed, reviewed
□ Rollback and forward-compatible schema strategy are rehearsed
□ Context-aware incident runbooks avoid destructive improvisation

callouts.title: Kubernetes Moves Failure; It Does Not Remove It
callouts.text: Reconciliation improves automation, but applications still need idempotency, timeouts, backpressure, graceful shutdown, data recovery, security, and observability.
